declarations.name: SafeLearning.CompleteModulesLandscapeSource91ARPartI.source_stability_interval_is_exactly_the_strict_absolute_multiplier_condition
declarations.signature:
theorem source_stability_interval_is_exactly_the_strict_absolute_multiplier_condition (k : ℝ) :
    (0 < k ∧ k < 2) ↔ |1-k| < 1

declarations.name: SafeLearning.CompleteModulesLandscapeSource91ARPartI.actual_centered_infinite_state_has_the_printed_initial_value_and_recursion
declarations.signature:
theorem actual_centered_infinite_state_has_the_printed_initial_value_and_recursion
    (k goal sigma : ℝ) (w : ℕ → ℝ) :
    infiniteTrajectory k goal sigma w 0-goal = -goal ∧
      ∀ t : ℕ, infiniteTrajectory k goal sigma w (t+1)-goal =
        (1-k)*(infiniteTrajectory k goal sigma w t-goal)+sigma*w t

declarations.name: SafeLearning.CompleteModulesLandscapeSource91ARPartI.actual_first_two_centered_substitutions_are_the_printed_values
declarations.signature:
theorem actual_first_two_centered_substitutions_are_the_printed_values
    (k goal sigma : ℝ) (w : ℕ → ℝ) :
    infiniteTrajectory k goal sigma w 1-goal = (1-k)*(-goal)+sigma*w 0 ∧
      infiniteTrajectory k goal sigma w 2-goal =
        (1-k)^2*(-goal)+sigma*((1-k)*w 0+w 1)

declarations.name: SafeLearning.CompleteModulesLandscapeSource91ARPartI.actual_centered_infinite_state_has_the_printed_unrolled_finite_sum
declarations.signature:
theorem actual_centered_infinite_state_has_the_printed_unrolled_finite_sum
    (k goal sigma : ℝ) (w : ℕ → ℝ) (t : ℕ) :
    infiniteTrajectory k goal sigma w t-goal =
      (1-k)^t*(-goal)+sigma*∑ j ∈ Finset.range t, (1-k)^(t-1-j)*w j

declarations.name: SafeLearning.CompleteModulesLandscapeSource91ARPartI.actual_infinite_standard_noise_has_zero_mean_and_unit_variance
declarations.signature:
theorem actual_infinite_standard_noise_has_zero_mean_and_unit_variance (t : ℕ) :
    (∫ w, w t ∂infiniteNoiseLaw) = 0 ∧
      Var[fun w => w t; infiniteNoiseLaw] = 1

declarations.name: SafeLearning.CompleteModulesLandscapeSource91ARPartI.actual_distinct_infinite_noise_cross_covariances_are_zero
declarations.signature:
theorem actual_distinct_infinite_noise_cross_covariances_are_zero
    (s t : ℕ) (hst : s ≠ t) :
    cov[fun w => w s, fun w => w t; infiniteNoiseLaw] = 0

declarations.name: SafeLearning.CompleteModulesLandscapeSource91ARPartI.actual_infinite_state_has_the_same_internally_derived_gaussian_marginal
declarations.signature:
theorem actual_infinite_state_has_the_same_internally_derived_gaussian_marginal
    (k goal sigma : ℝ) (t : ℕ) :
    HasLaw (fun w : ℕ → ℝ => infiniteTrajectory k goal sigma w t)
      (gaussianReal (trueMean k goal t) (trueVariance k sigma t).toNNReal) infiniteNoiseLaw

declarations.name: SafeLearning.CompleteModulesLandscapeSource91ARPartI.actual_infinite_state_mean_and_variance_are_the_printed_finite_formulas
declarations.signature:
theorem actual_infinite_state_mean_and_variance_are_the_printed_finite_formulas
    (k goal sigma : ℝ) (t : ℕ) :
    (∫ w, infiniteTrajectory k goal sigma w t ∂infiniteNoiseLaw) = goal*(1-(1-k)^t) ∧
      Var[fun w => infiniteTrajectory k goal sigma w t; infiniteNoiseLaw] =
        sigma^2*∑ i ∈ Finset.range t, (1-k)^(2*i)

declarations.name: SafeLearning.CompleteModulesLandscapeSource91ARPartI.the_two_printed_variance_sums_are_equal
declarations.signature:
theorem the_two_printed_variance_sums_are_equal (k sigma : ℝ) (t : ℕ) :
    sigma^2*(∑ j ∈ Finset.range t, (1-k)^(2*(t-1-j))) =
      sigma^2*(∑ i ∈ Finset.range t, (1-k)^(2*i))

declarations.name: SafeLearning.CompleteModulesLandscapeSource91ARPartI.the_printed_denominator_factorization_is_positive_on_the_source_stability_interval
declarations.signature:
theorem the_printed_denominator_factorization_is_positive_on_the_source_stability_interval
    (k : ℝ) (hk : 0 < k) (hk2 : k < 2) :
    1-(1-k)^2 = k*(2-k) ∧ 0 < k*(2-k)

declarations.name: SafeLearning.CompleteModulesLandscapeSource91ARPartI.actual_states_on_one_infinite_noise_space_converge_in_distribution_to_the_stationary_law
declarations.signature:
theorem actual_states_on_one_infinite_noise_space_converge_in_distribution_to_the_stationary_law
    (k goal sigma : ℝ) (hk : 0 < k) (hk2 : k < 2) :

theorem actual_gaussian_probability_measures_converge_weakly_with_their_parameters

theorem actual_recursive_states_converge_in_the_official_distribution_sense

theorem actual_recursive_marginals_converge_against_every_bounded_continuous_observable

declarations.name: SafeLearning.CompleteModulesLandscapeARPathFluctuation.actual_infinite_trajectory_satisfies_the_literal_initial_condition_and_recursion
declarations.signature:
theorem actual_infinite_trajectory_satisfies_the_literal_initial_condition_and_recursion
    (k goal sigma : ℝ) (w : ℕ → ℝ) :
    infiniteTrajectory k goal sigma w 0=0 ∧ ∀ t : ℕ,

theorem actual_infinite_trajectory_agrees_with_every_existing_finite_horizon_prefix

declarations.name: SafeLearning.CompleteModulesLandscapeARGaussianAlgebra.actual_trajectory_satisfies_the_literal_initial_condition_and_source_recursion
declarations.signature:
theorem actual_trajectory_satisfies_the_literal_initial_condition_and_source_recursion

declarations.name: SafeLearning.CompleteModulesLandscapeARGaussianAlgebra.actual_finite_vector_trajectory_is_the_affine_matrix_map
declarations.signature:

declarations.name: SafeLearning.CompleteModulesLandscapeARGaussianAlgebra.actual_squared_impulse_weights_sum_to_the_printed_variance

declarations.name: SafeLearning.CompleteModulesLandscapeARGaussianAlgebra.actual_earlier_and_later_impulse_weights_have_the_printed_covariance_product
declarations.signature:
theorem actual_earlier_and_later_impulse_weights_have_the_printed_covariance_product

declarations.name: SafeLearning.CompleteModulesLandscapeARGaussianAlgebra.actual_affine_design_gram_is_the_true_temporal_covariance

declarations.name: SafeLearning.CompleteModulesLandscapeARGaussianLaw.actual_recursive_trajectory_has_the_printed_temporal_covariance
declarations.signature:

claims.statement_in_prose: The centered initial state is -goal and e(t+1)=(1-k)e(t)+sigma*w(t).
actual_hypotheses: k, goal, sigma are arbitrary reals; w is an arbitrary real noise sequence.
claims.correspondence: The primitive recursive infiniteTrajectory literally starts at zero and uses the printed update. Subtraction and ring prove the centered initial value and recurrence; no desired centered recursion is assumed.

claims.statement_in_prose: The source condition 0<k<2 is equivalent to |1-k|<1.
actual_hypotheses: k is real; no one-sided stability hypothesis is assumed in the equivalence.
claims.correspondence: Both real inequalities are proved in both directions by abs_lt and linear arithmetic. The source abbreviation a=1-k preserves the exact strict inequalities.

claims.statement_in_prose: The first two centered states equal a*e(0)+sigma*w(0) and a^2*e(0)+sigma*(a*w(0)+w(1)).
actual_hypotheses: Arbitrary real k, goal, sigma and real sequence w.
claims.correspondence: The two conjuncts unfold the actual original recurrence at times one and two, then ring. e0=-goal, so both intermediate substitutions match the source.

claims.statement_in_prose: For every natural t the centered state is a^t*(-goal)+sigma*sum(j<t,a^(t-1-j)*w(j)).
actual_hypotheses: Arbitrary real parameters and w; every t in Nat, including zero.
claims.correspondence: The actual infinite path equals its finite prefix at horizon t. The finite affine trajectory theorem supplies the impulse coefficients; the explicitly typed finite-range sum and real algebra supply the printed sigma-times-sum expression. No recurrence solution or target formula is postulated.

claims.statement_in_prose: Each standard Gaussian noise has mean zero and variance one; distinct noise cross-covariances vanish.
actual_hypotheses: Normalized infinite product of standard Gaussian laws; distinct indices s!=t for cross-covariance.
claims.correspondence: Actual coordinate HasLaw gives zero means, unit variances and L2 membership. Actual iIndepFun gives independence for each distinct pair, then covariance_eq_zero. The independence and finite second moments are proved from the measure rather than left as an unexplained noise assumption.

claims.statement_in_prose: The original state has mean goal*(1-a^t) and variance sigma^2*sum(i<t,a^(2*i)).
actual_hypotheses: Canonical infinite standard Gaussian noise measure; arbitrary real parameters and every natural time.
claims.correspondence: Finite-prefix HasLaw composition transports the actual finite recursive Gaussian marginal to the same infinite path. Its integral and true variance give the printed mean and forward sum. Nonnegative trueVariance justifies toNNReal without clipping. sum_range_reflect proves the backward sum equality, with an empty sum at t=0.

claims.statement_in_prose: Under 0<k<2, 1-a^2=k*(2-k)>0 and the geometric ratio a^2 is below one.
claims.correspondence: The wrapper proves 1-a^2=k(2-k)>0. Therefore a^2<1 by subtraction, with a^2>=0 from square nonnegativity. Expanding either polynomial gives 2k-k^2, the intermediate factorization in the prose. StableMoments' actual geometric proof uses geom_sum_mul_neg and pow_mul, not an assumed closed formula.

claims.statement_in_prose: The variance equals sigma^2*(1-(1-k)^(2*t))/(k*(2-k)); it converges to sigma^2/(k*(2-k)), and the mean converges to goal.
actual_hypotheses: 0<k<2; arbitrary real goal and sigma; actual infinite-path moments already identified.
claims.correspondence: The finite sum is proved equal to the closed expression after proving the denominator nonzero. The strict absolute multiplier bound gives power convergence and the actual mean limit; the square ratio bound gives the variance limit. Negative multipliers for 1<k<2 are included. Sigma=0 and t=0 are valid without division by a standard deviation.

claims.statement_in_prose: Updating a mean-goal Gaussian state with independent standard noise produces variance a^2*v+sigma^2 and the same mean.
actual_hypotheses: Gaussian state has mean goal and variance v:NNReal; fresh noise is independent standard Gaussian; arbitrary real gain and sigma.
claims.correspondence: The actual independent product measure supplies the state and fresh noise laws. Scaling, independent Gaussian addition, and the constant shift derive a Gaussian of mean goal and variance (1-k)^2*v+sigma^2. This is a substitution test for a stationary law, not an assumption that the initial zero state is already stationary.

claims.statement_in_prose: The updated mean-goal Gaussian law is unchanged exactly for v=sigma^2/(1-a^2).
actual_hypotheses: 0<k<2; v>=0; independent fresh standard Gaussian noise and a Gaussian state of mean goal.
claims.correspondence: Gaussian extensionality proves invariance iff the actual variance update is fixed. Positive k(2-k) then proves both directions of v=sigma^2/[k(2-k)]; the wrapper identifies this denominator with 1-a^2. Existing StationaryGaussian constructs this normalized law and proves its actual one-step invariance. This is uniqueness among mean-goal Gaussian laws, not arbitrary invariant measures.

claims.statement_in_prose: The original states converge in distribution to the stated stationary Gaussian law.
actual_hypotheses: 0<k<2; all states use the one infinite independent Gaussian measure.
claims.correspondence: The wrapper explicitly equates each infinite state pushforward to the internally derived finite actualTimeLaw, then transports actual characteristic-function convergence into the official TendstoInDistribution statement. The limit is the independently verified stationary Gaussian. Changing finite spaces are intermediate models, not the path process used in the final conclusion.

claims.statement_in_prose: For sigma>0 individual noisy trajectories do not settle at the goal.
actual_hypotheses: sigma>0 in the source, which implies the theorem's sigma!=0; no gain restriction is needed for this stronger path conclusion.
claims.correspondence: Positive Gaussian probabilities of >1 and <-1 are derived via mutual absolute continuity with volume. Independent coordinate events have divergent probability sums; second Borel-Cantelli puts both repeated crossings on a single almost-sure event. This excludes every finite noise limit on that event. Actual recurrence algebra shows any finite state-path limit would force a finite noise limit. Consequently the noisy state cannot converge to goal almost surely. No uncountable intersection of null sets is used.
